> **Practice spec for the Luca v1 tracer bullet. Throwaway: its PR is never merged.** See [Tracer bullet: build one real ticket end to end with Claude Code agents](https://github.com/asibilia/luca-framework/issues/334).

## Problem Statement

Code in this repo sometimes needs to turn a title, like a ticket's name, into a short, URL-safe name for a branch, a folder, or a file. Doing it by hand gives messy results: capital letters, spaces, accents, and stray symbols.

## Solution

A small `slugify` helper that turns any text into a clean slug: lowercase ASCII letters and digits, with single dashes between words, and an optional length limit.

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want "Hello World" to become "hello-world", so that I can use titles in URLs and branch names.
2. As a developer, I want accented letters turned into plain letters, so that slugs stay ASCII.
3. As a developer, I want runs of spaces, dashes, and symbols collapsed into one dash, so that slugs look clean.
4. As a developer, I want no dash at the start or end of a slug, so that slugs join cleanly with other names.
5. As a developer, I want text with no letters or digits to give an empty slug, so that I can detect it and fall back.
6. As a developer, I want to cap a slug's length without leaving a dash at the end, so that it fits length limits.

## Implementation Decisions

- A new scratch package, `tracer-sandbox`, holds one module that exports `slugify(text, options?)`.
- `options.maxLength` is optional. Without it, the whole slug is returned.
- Accents are removed with Unicode NFKD normalization, dropping the combining marks. Any other non-ASCII character is dropped.
- No dependencies.

## Testing Decisions

- Test only the public `slugify` function, through its inputs and outputs. No mocks.
- Unit tests sit next to the module and run with `bun test`.
- Each acceptance criterion gets at least one test.
- Prior art: none in this repo yet. This is the first package since old Luca was removed.

## Out of Scope

- Transliterating non-Latin scripts. Their characters are dropped.
- Custom separators.
- Publishing the package.

## Further Notes

- Built by the Luca v1 tracer bullet. Its PR is a draft that gets closed, never merged.

tickets.body:
## Parent

#351 (Practice spec: slugify helper)

## What to build

A developer can call `slugify(text)` from the new `tracer-sandbox` package and get a clean, URL-safe slug, with an optional `maxLength`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `slugify("Hello World")` returns `"hello-world"`.
- [ ] Accented letters become plain letters: `slugify("Crème Brûlée")` returns `"creme-brulee"`.
- [ ] Runs of spaces, dashes, and symbols become one dash, with none at the start or end: `slugify("  --Hello,   World!--  ")` returns `"hello-world"`.
- [ ] Text with no letters or digits gives an empty slug: `slugify("!!!")` and `slugify("")` both return `""`.
- [ ] `maxLength` cuts the slug without leaving a dash at the end: `slugify("Hello World Again", { maxLength: 12 })` returns `"hello-world"`.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

# Your role: test-writer (Luca engine, tracer bullet)

You write the failing tests for ONE ticket, before any code exists. Plain code (the engine) drives this run and checks your work.

Rules:
- Create or edit ONLY test files matching **/*.test.ts. No other file: no implementation, no package.json, no config, no notes. The engine reverts anything else and counts it as a failed try.
- Your new tests must FAIL right now, because the code does not exist yet. That is expected. Do not create or stub the module under test.
- Test only the public behavior the ticket names, at the seams the spec's "Testing Decisions" section names. No mocks unless the spec asks. No tautological asserts.
- Every acceptance criterion needs at least one test. Name tests so a reader can tell which criterion each checks.
- Old tests must keep passing. Don't edit or delete existing tests unless the ticket requires it.
- Use bun's test runner: import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test". You may run `bun test` yourself; only the engine's own run counts.
- Give every test a plain string-literal name (no test.each, no template names), so the engine can find each named test even before the module exists.
- If the engine sends you review findings about tests, fix them in the test files. For a finding you disagree with, list it under "wont_fix" with your reason.
- Never commit, stage, stash, branch, reset, push, or touch GitHub. The engine owns every git and GitHub side effect. Network is off.
- If something is unclear, make your best call and list it under "assumptions". Don't stop to ask.
- "run_notes": at most 3 short facts about this repo that would help later agents in this run. Can be empty.
- You may send a one-way heads-up to another live agent with the send_message tool. It's rarely needed; nobody replies.

Your result (structured output):
- outcome: "tests_written", or "nothing_new_to_test" if the ticket truly changes no behavior (a refactor).
- criteria: for EACH criterion id (AC1, AC2, ...), the tests that check it, as { file, name }. "name" is the full name bun prints: describe names and the test name joined by " > ".
- summary, wont_fix (usually empty), assumptions, run_notes.

## Ticket #352: Add a slugify helper

## Parent

#351 (Practice spec: slugify helper)

## What to build

A developer can call `slugify(text)` from the new `tracer-sandbox` package and get a clean, URL-safe slug, with an optional `maxLength`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `slugify("Hello World")` returns `"hello-world"`.
- [ ] Accented letters become plain letters: `slugify("Crème Brûlée")` returns `"creme-brulee"`.
- [ ] Runs of spaces, dashes, and symbols become one dash, with none at the start or end: `slugify("  --Hello,   World!--  ")` returns `"hello-world"`.
- [ ] Text with no letters or digits gives an empty slug: `slugify("!!!")` and `slugify("")` both return `""`.
- [ ] `maxLength` cuts the slug without leaving a dash at the end: `slugify("Hello World Again", { maxLength: 12 })` returns `"hello-world"`.

## Blocked by

## Spec #351: Practice spec: slugify helper (tracer bullet, throwaway)

> **Practice spec for the Luca v1 tracer bullet. Throwaway: its PR is never merged.** See [Tracer bullet: build one real ticket end to end with Claude Code agents](https://github.com/asibilia/luca-framework/issues/334).

## Problem Statement

Code in this repo sometimes needs to turn a title, like a ticket's name, into a short, URL-safe name for a branch, a folder, or a file. Doing it by hand gives messy results: capital letters, spaces, accents, and stray symbols.

## Solution

A small `slugify` helper that turns any text into a clean slug: lowercase ASCII letters and digits, with single dashes between words, and an optional length limit.

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want "Hello World" to become "hello-world", so that I can use titles in URLs and branch names.
2. As a developer, I want accented letters turned into plain letters, so that slugs stay ASCII.
3. As a developer, I want runs of spaces, dashes, and symbols collapsed into one dash, so that slugs look clean.
4. As a developer, I want no dash at the start or end of a slug, so that slugs join cleanly with other names.
5. As a developer, I want text with no letters or digits to give an empty slug, so that I can detect it and fall back.
6. As a developer, I want to cap a slug's length without leaving a dash at the end, so that it fits length limits.

## Implementation Decisions

- A new scratch package, `tracer-sandbox`, holds one module that exports `slugify(text, options?)`.
- `options.maxLength` is optional. Without it, the whole slug is returned.
- Accents are removed with Unicode NFKD normalization, dropping the combining marks. Any other non-ASCII character is dropped.
- No dependencies.

## Testing Decisions

- Test only the public `slugify` function, through its inputs and outputs. No mocks.
- Unit tests sit next to the module and run with `bun test`.
- Each acceptance criterion gets at least one test.
- Prior art: none in this repo yet. This is the first package since old Luca was removed.

## Out of Scope

- Transliterating non-Latin scripts. Their characters are dropped.
- Custom separators.
- Publishing the package.

- Built by the Luca v1 tracer bullet. Its PR is a draft that gets closed, never merged.

+export interface SlugifyOptions {
+  /** Longest slug to return. The cut never leaves a dash at the end. */
+  maxLength?: number;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Turns text into a URL-safe slug: lowercase ASCII letters and digits with
+ * single dashes between words. Accents are stripped via NFKD; any other
+ * non-ASCII character is dropped.
+ */
+export function slugify(text: string, options: SlugifyOptions = {}): string {
+  const slug = text
+    .normalize("NFKD")
+    .replace(/\p{M}/gu, "")
+    .replace(/[^\x00-\x7F]/g, "")
+    .toLowerCase()
+    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-")
+    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "");
+
+  if (options.maxLength === undefined) return slug;
+  return slug.slice(0, Math.max(0, options.maxLength)).replace(/-+$/, "");

## Ticket #352: Add a slugify helper

## Parent

#351 (Practice spec: slugify helper)

## What to build

A developer can call `slugify(text)` from the new `tracer-sandbox` package and get a clean, URL-safe slug, with an optional `maxLength`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `slugify("Hello World")` returns `"hello-world"`.
- [ ] Accented letters become plain letters: `slugify("Crème Brûlée")` returns `"creme-brulee"`.
- [ ] Runs of spaces, dashes, and symbols become one dash, with none at the start or end: `slugify("  --Hello,   World!--  ")` returns `"hello-world"`.
- [ ] Text with no letters or digits gives an empty slug: `slugify("!!!")` and `slugify("")` both return `""`.
- [ ] `maxLength` cuts the slug without leaving a dash at the end: `slugify("Hello World Again", { maxLength: 12 })` returns `"hello-world"`.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Spec #351: Practice spec: slugify helper (tracer bullet, throwaway)

> **Practice spec for the Luca v1 tracer bullet. Throwaway: its PR is never merged.** See [Tracer bullet: build one real ticket end to end with Claude Code agents](https://github.com/asibilia/luca-framework/issues/334).

## Problem Statement

Code in this repo sometimes needs to turn a title, like a ticket's name, into a short, URL-safe name for a branch, a folder, or a file. Doing it by hand gives messy results: capital letters, spaces, accents, and stray symbols.

## Solution

A small `slugify` helper that turns any text into a clean slug: lowercase ASCII letters and digits, with single dashes between words, and an optional length limit.

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want "Hello World" to become "hello-world", so that I can use titles in URLs and branch names.
2. As a developer, I want accented letters turned into plain letters, so that slugs stay ASCII.
3. As a developer, I want runs of spaces, dashes, and symbols collapsed into one dash, so that slugs look clean.
4. As a developer, I want no dash at the start or end of a slug, so that slugs join cleanly with other names.
5. As a developer, I want text with no letters or digits to give an empty slug, so that I can detect it and fall back.
6. As a developer, I want to cap a slug's length without leaving a dash at the end, so that it fits length limits.

## Implementation Decisions

- A new scratch package, `tracer-sandbox`, holds one module that exports `slugify(text, options?)`.
- `options.maxLength` is optional. Without it, the whole slug is returned.
- Accents are removed with Unicode NFKD normalization, dropping the combining marks. Any other non-ASCII character is dropped.
- No dependencies.

## Testing Decisions

- Test only the public `slugify` function, through its inputs and outputs. No mocks.
- Unit tests sit next to the module and run with `bun test`.
- Each acceptance criterion gets at least one test.
- Prior art: none in this repo yet. This is the first package since old Luca was removed.

## Out of Scope

- Transliterating non-Latin scripts. Their characters are dropped.
- Custom separators.
- Publishing the package.

- Built by the Luca v1 tracer bullet. Its PR is a draft that gets closed, never merged.

content.text: I've finished reviewing; filing the result now.

criteria.evidence: The chain lowercases, turns each run of non-[a-z0-9] characters into one '-', and trims the ends, so "Hello World" becomes "hello-world". Test 'AC1' checks this and passes.

normalize('NFKD') splits è/û/é into a base letter plus a combining mark, and /\p{M}/gu removes the marks, giving "creme-brulee". Test 'AC2' checks this and passes. It would fail if the marks weren't stripped, because the non-ASCII drop alone would give "crme-brle".
/[^a-z0-9]+/g → '-' collapses each run, then /^-+|-+$/g trims the ends, so the input becomes "hello-world". Test 'AC3' uses the exact input from the criterion and passes.
"!!!" becomes "-", which the trim empties. "" stays "". There is one test for each, and both pass.

"hello-world-again".slice(0,12) gives "hello-world-", and /-+$/ strips the dash to give "hello-world". Tests cover the exact case from the criterion, a cut that ends on a letter (maxLength 8 → "hello-wo"), and the case with no maxLength. All pass (bun test: 8 pass, 0 fail).

findings.title: slugify.ts breaks the repo's lint rules (prettier style and no-control-regex)
findings.detail: In eslint.config.mjs, 'prettier/prettier' is set to 'error' with semi:false, singleQuote:true, tabWidth:4. The existing TS in the repo follows that style (see commit.config.ts). slugify.ts uses double quotes, semicolons, and 2-space indent, so `bun run lint` will report errors. Also, js.configs.recommended turns on no-control-regex, which flags the `\x00` in /[^\x00-\x7F]/g. Reformat to the repo style. Replace the ASCII filter with an equivalent that avoids the control character, such as /[^\p{ASCII}]/gu. Don't narrow it to \x20-\x7E: that would silently drop tabs and newlines instead of turning them into dashes.

findings.title: The test file also breaks the repo's prettier style
findings.detail: It uses double quotes, semicolons, and 2-space indent, while the repo's prettier/prettier rule (an error) requires single quotes, no semicolons, and 4-space indent. `bun run lint` will report errors here too. Reformat it to match.

findings.title: No test for the 'other non-ASCII is dropped' decision
findings.detail: The spec's Implementation Decisions say that non-ASCII characters without a plain-letter form are dropped, not turned into dashes. It isn't an acceptance criterion, but one test such as slugify('a✓b') === 'ab' or slugify('日本 Tokyo') === 'tokyo' would lock it in. Without the /[^\x00-\x7F]/ step, 'a✓b' would become 'a-b'.

findings.title: bun.lock doesn't list the new workspace
findings.detail: The implementer noted that `bun install` was denied, so bun.lock was never updated for packages/tracer-sandbox. A frozen-lockfile install would fail. Run `bun install` and commit the lockfile if the environment allows it.

## Ticket #352: Add a slugify helper

## Parent

#351 (Practice spec: slugify helper)

## What to build

A developer can call `slugify(text)` from the new `tracer-sandbox` package and get a clean, URL-safe slug, with an optional `maxLength`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `slugify("Hello World")` returns `"hello-world"`.
- [ ] Accented letters become plain letters: `slugify("Crème Brûlée")` returns `"creme-brulee"`.
- [ ] Runs of spaces, dashes, and symbols become one dash, with none at the start or end: `slugify("  --Hello,   World!--  ")` returns `"hello-world"`.
- [ ] Text with no letters or digits gives an empty slug: `slugify("!!!")` and `slugify("")` both return `""`.
- [ ] `maxLength` cuts the slug without leaving a dash at the end: `slugify("Hello World Again", { maxLength: 12 })` returns `"hello-world"`.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Spec #351: Practice spec: slugify helper (tracer bullet, throwaway)

> **Practice spec for the Luca v1 tracer bullet. Throwaway: its PR is never merged.** See [Tracer bullet: build one real ticket end to end with Claude Code agents](https://github.com/asibilia/luca-framework/issues/334).

## Problem Statement

Code in this repo sometimes needs to turn a title, like a ticket's name, into a short, URL-safe name for a branch, a folder, or a file. Doing it by hand gives messy results: capital letters, spaces, accents, and stray symbols.

## Solution

A small `slugify` helper that turns any text into a clean slug: lowercase ASCII letters and digits, with single dashes between words, and an optional length limit.

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want "Hello World" to become "hello-world", so that I can use titles in URLs and branch names.
2. As a developer, I want accented letters turned into plain letters, so that slugs stay ASCII.
3. As a developer, I want runs of spaces, dashes, and symbols collapsed into one dash, so that slugs look clean.
4. As a developer, I want no dash at the start or end of a slug, so that slugs join cleanly with other names.
5. As a developer, I want text with no letters or digits to give an empty slug, so that I can detect it and fall back.
6. As a developer, I want to cap a slug's length without leaving a dash at the end, so that it fits length limits.

## Implementation Decisions

- A new scratch package, `tracer-sandbox`, holds one module that exports `slugify(text, options?)`.
- `options.maxLength` is optional. Without it, the whole slug is returned.
- Accents are removed with Unicode NFKD normalization, dropping the combining marks. Any other non-ASCII character is dropped.
- No dependencies.

## Testing Decisions

- Test only the public `slugify` function, through its inputs and outputs. No mocks.
- Unit tests sit next to the module and run with `bun test`.
- Each acceptance criterion gets at least one test.
- Prior art: none in this repo yet. This is the first package since old Luca was removed.

## Out of Scope

- Transliterating non-Latin scripts. Their characters are dropped.
- Custom separators.
- Publishing the package.

## Further Notes

- Built by the Luca v1 tracer bullet. Its PR is a draft that gets closed, never merged.

- **Old Luca is gone.** The `luca` CLI and its packages (`packages/luca`, `luca-cli`, `luca-core`, `luca-tools`, `luca-code`) have been deleted, along with the npm release workflow and changesets. It isn't an acceptance criterion, but one test such as slugify('a✓b') === 'ab' or slugify('日本 Tokyo') === 'tokyo' would lock it in. Without the /[^\x00-\x7F]/ step, 'a✓b' would become 'a-b'.

## Acceptance criteria
AC1: `slugify("Hello World")` returns `"hello-world"`.
AC2: Accented letters become plain letters: `slugify("Crème Brûlée")` returns `"creme-brulee"`.
AC3: Runs of spaces, dashes, and symbols become one dash, with none at the start or end: `slugify("  --Hello,   World!--  ")` returns `"hello-world"`.
AC4: Text with no letters or digits gives an empty slug: `slugify("!!!")` and `slugify("")` both return `""`.
AC5: `maxLength` cuts the slug without leaving a dash at the end: `slugify("Hello World Again", { maxLength: 12 })` returns `"hello-world"`.

## Earlier findings and the fixers' responses
- R1-1 [should_fix, code] packages/tracer-sandbox/src/slugify.ts: slugify.ts breaks the repo's lint rules (prettier style and no-control-regex). In eslint.config.mjs, 'prettier/prettier' is set to 'error' with semi:false, singleQuote:true, tabWidth:4. The existing TS in the repo follows that style (see commit.config.ts). slugify.ts uses double quotes, semicolons, and 2-space indent, so `bun run lint` will report errors. Also, js.configs.recommended turns on no-control-regex, which flags the `\x00` in /[^\x00-\x7F]/g. Reformat to the repo style. Replace the ASCII filter with an equivalent that avoids the control character, such as /[^\p{ASCII}]/gu. Don't narrow it to \x20-\x7E: that would silently drop tabs and newlines instead of turning them into dashes.

Reformat it to match.

## Ticket #352: Add a slugify helper

## Parent

#351 (Practice spec: slugify helper)

## What to build

A developer can call `slugify(text)` from the new `tracer-sandbox` package and get a clean, URL-safe slug, with an optional `maxLength`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `slugify("Hello World")` returns `"hello-world"`.
- [ ] Accented letters become plain letters: `slugify("Crème Brûlée")` returns `"creme-brulee"`.
- [ ] Runs of spaces, dashes, and symbols become one dash, with none at the start or end: `slugify("  --Hello,   World!--  ")` returns `"hello-world"`.
- [ ] Text with no letters or digits gives an empty slug: `slugify("!!!")` and `slugify("")` both return `""`.
- [ ] `maxLength` cuts the slug without leaving a dash at the end: `slugify("Hello World Again", { maxLength: 12 })` returns `"hello-world"`.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Spec #351: Practice spec: slugify helper (tracer bullet, throwaway)

> **Practice spec for the Luca v1 tracer bullet. Throwaway: its PR is never merged.** See [Tracer bullet: build one real ticket end to end with Claude Code agents](https://github.com/asibilia/luca-framework/issues/334).

## Problem Statement

Code in this repo sometimes needs to turn a title, like a ticket's name, into a short, URL-safe name for a branch, a folder, or a file. Doing it by hand gives messy results: capital letters, spaces, accents, and stray symbols.

## Solution

A small `slugify` helper that turns any text into a clean slug: lowercase ASCII letters and digits, with single dashes between words, and an optional length limit.

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want "Hello World" to become "hello-world", so that I can use titles in URLs and branch names.
2. As a developer, I want accented letters turned into plain letters, so that slugs stay ASCII.
3. As a developer, I want runs of spaces, dashes, and symbols collapsed into one dash, so that slugs look clean.
4. As a developer, I want no dash at the start or end of a slug, so that slugs join cleanly with other names.
5. As a developer, I want text with no letters or digits to give an empty slug, so that I can detect it and fall back.
6. As a developer, I want to cap a slug's length without leaving a dash at the end, so that it fits length limits.

## Implementation Decisions

- A new scratch package, `tracer-sandbox`, holds one module that exports `slugify(text, options?)`.
- `options.maxLength` is optional. Without it, the whole slug is returned.
- Accents are removed with Unicode NFKD normalization, dropping the combining marks. Any other non-ASCII character is dropped.
- No dependencies.

## Testing Decisions

- Test only the public `slugify` function, through its inputs and outputs. No mocks.
- Unit tests sit next to the module and run with `bun test`.
- Each acceptance criterion gets at least one test.
- Prior art: none in this repo yet. This is the first package since old Luca was removed.

## Out of Scope

- Transliterating non-Latin scripts. Their characters are dropped.
- Custom separators.
- Publishing the package.

## Further Notes

- Built by the Luca v1 tracer bullet. Its PR is a draft that gets closed, never merged.

criteria.evidence: The code change is formatting only, so the pipeline behaves as before. The test 'AC1' expects slugify('Hello World') to be 'hello-world' and passes (bun test: 8 pass, 0 fail).

The code still runs NFKD, then strips \p{M}, then drops non-ASCII characters. `/[^\p{ASCII}]/gu` matches the same set as the old `/[^\x00-\x7F]/g`. The test expects 'Crème Brûlée' to become 'creme-brulee' and passes.
The code replaces `/[^a-z0-9]+/g` with '-', then trims leading and trailing dashes with `/^-+|-+$/g`. The test for '  --Hello,   World!--  ' expects 'hello-world' and passes.
Two tests cover this: '!!!' and '' both return '', and both pass.

The code slices to maxLength, then strips trailing dashes with `.replace(/-+$/, '')`. maxLength 12 gives 'hello-world'. maxLength 8 gives 'hello-wo', and with no maxLength the whole slug comes back. That rules out an implementation that always strips the last segment. All three tests pass.

earlier_findings.note: slugify.ts now uses 4-space indent, single quotes, and no semicolons, which matches the prettier/prettier options in eslint.config.mjs. The ASCII filter is now `/[^\p{ASCII}]/gu`. That avoids the no-control-regex hit and keeps the full U+0000–U+007F range, so tabs and newlines still turn into dashes.

slugify.test.ts is reformatted to single quotes, no semicolons, and 4-space indent. The one call too long for printWidth 80 (the maxLength 12 case, 83 columns) is wrapped the way prettier would wrap it, with no trailing comma on the call argument under es5. The long test() titles are fine because prettier keeps test-call titles on one line.

state.implementer_summary: Fixed R1-1 in packages/tracer-sandbox/src/slugify.ts. The file now follows the repo's prettier style: 4-space indent, single quotes, no semicolons, and every line is under 80 characters. The ASCII filter /[^\x00-\x7F]/g is now /[^\p{ASCII}]/gu. It keeps the same range but has no control character, so no-control-regex won't flag it. Tabs and newlines still become dashes. Both gates pass: `bun test` ran 8 tests with 0 failures, and `bunx --bun tsc --noEmit` found no errors. I couldn't run the linter because the session denied `bun run lint`. I checked the style by hand against the rules in eslint.config.mjs.

criteria.evidence: The code change is formatting only, so the pipeline behaves as before. The test 'AC1' expects slugify('Hello World') to be 'hello-world' and passes (bun test: 8 pass, 0 fail).

The code still runs NFKD, then strips \p{M}, then drops non-ASCII characters. `/[^\p{ASCII}]/gu` matches the same set as the old `/[^\x00-\x7F]/g`. The test expects 'Crème Brûlée' to become 'creme-brulee' and passes.
The code replaces `/[^a-z0-9]+/g` with '-', then trims leading and trailing dashes with `/^-+|-+$/g`. The test for '  --Hello,   World!--  ' expects 'hello-world' and passes.
Two tests cover this: '!!!' and '' both return '', and both pass.

The code slices to maxLength, then strips trailing dashes with `.replace(/-+$/, '')`. maxLength 12 gives 'hello-world'. maxLength 8 gives 'hello-wo', and with no maxLength the whole slug comes back. That rules out an implementation that always strips the last segment. All three tests pass.

nits.title: No test for the 'other non-ASCII is dropped' decision
nits.detail: The spec's Implementation Decisions say that non-ASCII characters without a plain-letter form are dropped, not turned into dashes. It isn't an acceptance criterion, but one test such as slugify('a✓b') === 'ab' or slugify('日本 Tokyo') === 'tokyo' would lock it in. Without the /[^\x00-\x7F]/ step, 'a✓b' would become 'a-b'.

nits.detail: The implementer noted that `bun install` was denied, so bun.lock was never updated for packages/tracer-sandbox. A frozen-lockfile install would fail. Run `bun install` and commit the lockfile if the environment allows it.

criteria.text: `slugify("Hello World")` returns `"hello-world"`.
Accented letters become plain letters: `slugify("Crème Brûlée")` returns `"creme-brulee"`.
Runs of spaces, dashes, and symbols become one dash, with none at the start or end: `slugify("  --Hello,   World!--  ")` returns `"hello-world"`.
Text with no letters or digits gives an empty slug: `slugify("!!!")` and `slugify("")` both return `""`.
`maxLength` cuts the slug without leaving a dash at the end: `slugify("Hello World Again", { maxLength: 12 })` returns `"hello-world"`.
